Θεὸν, ἑλκομένας δὲ τρόπον τινὰ παρ' αὐτῶν, διὰ τοῦ βούλεσθαι καὶ
τοῖς ἐκ θείας 70.160 ὀργῆς περιπεσεῖν κινήμασιν. Οἶμαι δὲ ἔγωγε τῶν τοιούτων
ἑκάστῳ πρεπωδέστατά τε καὶ ἀληθῶς δύνα- σθαι λέγειν ἡμᾶς· "6Ἢ τοῦ πλούτου τῆς
χρηστότητος αὐτοῦ, καὶ τῆς ἀνοχῆς, καὶ τῆς μακροθυμίας κατα- φρονεῖς, ἀγνοῶν
ὅτι τὸ χρηστὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰς μετά- νοιάν σε ἄγει; Κατὰ δὲ τὴν σκληρότητά σου καὶ
ἀμε- τανόητον καρδίαν θησαυρίζεις σεαυτῷ ὀργὴν, ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ὀργῆς καὶ
ἀποκαλύψεως καὶ δικαιοκρισίας τοῦ Θεοῦ."6 Ἕλκουσι γὰρ, ὡς ἔφην, αὐτοὶ καθ'
ἑαυτῶν τὸν τῆς κολάσεως καιρὸν, τάχα που μικροψυχοῦντες, ὅτι μέλλει κολάζων
αὐτοὺς, καὶ μὴ πλημμελοῦσιν ἀκαθέκτως ἐπετίθει τὰς δίκας. Ἕλκουσι τοίνυν τὰς
ἁμαρτίας ὡς σχοίνῳ μακρῷ, καὶ ὡς ζυγοῦ ἱμάντι δαμάλεως τὰς ἀνομίας. Ὥσπερ γὰρ
τὰς δαμάλεις, ἤτοι τὰς βοῦς ὑποφέροντες τοῖς ζυγοῖς, ἕλκουσιν ἔσθ' ὅτε σὺν βίᾳ
πολλῇ, καὶ καταδεσμεύουσιν εἰς πόνους· τὸν αὐτὸν, οἶμαι, τρόπον κἀκεῖνοι τοῖς ἐκ
θείας ὀρ- γῆς ἐπισυμβήσεσθαι μέλλουσιν ἑαυτοὺς ὑποφέροντες ἔφασκον·
"6Ἐγγισάτω τὸ τάχος, ἃ ποιήσει, ἵνα ἴδωμεν, καὶ ἐλθέτω ἡ βουλὴ τοῦ ἁγίου Ἰσραὴλ
ἵνα γνῶμεν."6 Τοῦτο λέγοντας καὶ οὕτω πεφρονηκότας καὶ ἕτερος τῶν ἁγίων
προφητῶν ταλανίζει λέγων· Οὐαὶ οἱ ἐπι- θυμοῦντες τὴν ἡμέραν Κυρίου· καὶ αὕτη
ἐστὶ σκότος, καὶ οὐ φῶς, καὶ γνόφος οὐκ ἔχων φέγγος αὐτοῦ. Χρὴ τοίνυν
μανθάνοντας ὅτι λελύπηται Θεὸς, παραχρῆμα μετανοεῖν, καὶ ἀκαταλήκτοις
προσευχαῖς μειλίσσεσθαι μᾶλλον αὐτὸν, οὐ παροτρύνειν ἔτι κεκινημένον· οὔτε μὴν
ἀπειλοῦντος καταφρονεῖν· μακρόθυμος γάρ ἐστι, καὶ πολυέλεος, ἀποφέρων ἀνομίας,
καὶ ὑπερ- βαίνων ἀδικίας· καὶ μικροῖς ἔσθ' ὅτε δακρύοις τῶν ἡμαρτηκότων ἐπὶ τὴν
αὐτῷ φιλαιτάτην γαληνότητα μεθιστάμενος. 9Οὐαὶ οἱ λέγοντες τὸ πονηρὸν
καλὸν, καὶ τὸ κα- λὸν πονηρὸν, οἱ τιθέντες τὸ σκότος φῶς, καὶ τὸ φῶς σκότος, οἱ
τιθέντες τὸ πικρὸν γλυκὺ, καὶ τὸ γλυκὺ πικρόν. Οὐαὶ οἱ συνετοὶ ἐν ἑαυτοῖς, καὶ
ἐνώπιον ἑαυτῶν ἐπιστήμονες.9 Ἀσυνέτους ὄντας παντελῶς καὶ διὰ τούτων ἐλέγχει
τοὺς τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἐπισπωμένους ὡς σχοινίῳ μακρῷ. ∆έον γὰρ ἐπαίνου παντὸς
ἀξιοῦν τὸ χρῆναι μετανοεῖν, καὶ διὰ πάσης ἐπιεικείας ἀπαλλάττειν ἑαυτοὺς τῆς
ἐπηρτημένης ὀργῆς, καὶ ταῖς νηστείαις ἀπολογεῖσθαι λελυπημένῳ τῷ πάντων
κρατοῦντι Θεῷ· ἀδόκιμοι γεγόνασι τραπεζῖται, τιμῶντες μὲν τὰ αἰσχίω, κατα-
κιβδηλεύοντες δὲ τὸ ἀσυγκρίτως ἄμεινον, καὶ τὸ ὅτι μάλιστα λυσιτελὲς εἰς 56 σωτηρίαν αὐτοῖς. Πρέπει δὴ οὖν ἄρα τοῖς οὕτω πεφρονηκόσι τὸ οὐαί. Ἀνόσιοι γὰρ
καὶ ἀσύνετοι καθ' ἑαυτῶν γεγόνασι δικασταί. Τὸ μὲν γὰρ πονηρὸν καλὸν εἶναι
λέγοντες, καταλογι- ζόμενοι τὸ σκότος φῶς, καὶ τὸ μὲν πικρὸν γλυκὺ, τὸ δὲ γλυκὺ

pass_a_gloss: [...] God, but being dragged in some manner by them, through wishing also to fall into the movements from divine wrath. And I for my part think we can say to each of such most fittingly and truly: Or do you despise the wealth of his kindness and forbearance and long-suffering, not knowing that the kindness of God leads you to repentance? But according to your hardness and unrepenting heart you store up for yourself wrath, in a day of wrath and revelation and just judgment of God. For they drag, as I said, upon themselves the time of the punishment, perhaps being petty that he delays punishing them, and was not laying on the penalties upon those offending without restraint. They drag then the sins as with a long rope, and the lawlessnesses as with a strap of a heifer's yoke. For just as those bringing the heifers, or the oxen, under the yokes drag them sometimes with much force, and bind them down into labours, in the same manner, I think, those too, bringing themselves under the things about to befall from divine wrath, were saying: Let what he will do draw near quickly, so that we may see, and let the counsel of the holy one of Israel come, so that we may know. Those saying this and thinking thus another of the holy prophets also laments, saying: Woe those desiring the day of the Lord; and this is darkness, and not light, and gloom not having its brightness. It is needed then, learning that God has been grieved, to repent immediately, and with unceasing prayers rather to soothe him, not to provoke him further when moved; nor yet to despise him threatening; for he is long-suffering and much-merciful, carrying off lawlessnesses, and passing over injustices; and sometimes at small tears of those who have sinned moving over to the calmness most dear to him. [Lemma, Isaiah 5:20-21:] Woe those saying the evil good, and the good evil, those setting the darkness light and the light darkness, those setting the bitter sweet and the sweet bitter. Woe those understanding in themselves, and knowing before themselves. He convicts through these too as wholly without understanding those dragging on the sins as with a long rope. For when it was needed to deem worthy of every praise the need to repent, and through every gentleness to free themselves from the wrath hanging over, and with the fasts to make defence to the grieved God who rules all, they became unapproved money-changers, honouring the more shameful things, and making counterfeit the incomparably better thing, and the very most profitable for salvation to them. Fitting then to those thinking thus is the woe. For unholy and senseless judges against themselves they have become. For saying the evil to be good, counting the darkness light, and the bitter sweet, and the sweet bi[tter] [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: … and yet in a way those punishments were being dragged on by them, because they wished to fall even into the outbursts of divine wrath. I think that we can say to each such person, most fittingly and truly: “Or do you despise the riches of his kindness and forbearance and patience, not knowing that God’s kindness is leading you to repentance? But by your hardness and impenitent heart you are storing up wrath for yourself on the day of wrath and of the revelation of the righteous judgment of God” (Romans 2:4–5).

For, as I said, they drag the time of punishment upon themselves, perhaps fretting that he was slow to punish them and was not laying penalties on them as they sinned without restraint. So they drag their sins as with a long rope, and their lawless deeds as with the strap of a heifer’s yoke. For just as those who bring heifers, that is, oxen, under the yoke sometimes drag them with great force and bind them to their labor, so in the same way, I think, these men too put themselves under what was about to befall them from divine wrath, and said: “Let what he will do come near quickly, so that we may see; and let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel come, so that we may know” (Isaiah 5:19).

Those who say this and think this way another of the holy prophets also calls wretched, saying: “Woe to those who long for the day of the Lord! It is darkness and not light, gloom that has no brightness” (Amos 5:18, 20).

So when we learn that God has been grieved, we must repent at once and soothe him instead with unceasing prayers, not provoke him further once he has been moved, nor despise him when he threatens. For he is patient and rich in mercy, taking away lawless deeds and passing over wrongs (compare Numbers 14:18; Micah 7:18), and sometimes, at the few tears of those who have sinned, he turns back to the calm that is dearest to him.

“Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who put darkness for light and light for darkness, who put bitter for sweet and sweet for bitter. Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes and clever in their own sight” (Isaiah 5:20–21).

By these words too he shows that those who drag their sins as with a long rope are utterly without understanding. When they ought to have counted the duty of repentance worthy of all praise, to free themselves by every kind of gentleness from the wrath hanging over them, and to make their defense with fasts before God, the ruler of all, whom they had grieved, they have become untrustworthy money-changers, valuing the baser things and debasing what is incomparably better and most profitable for their salvation.

So the “woe” fits those who think this way. For they have become unholy and senseless judges against themselves. By saying that evil is good, by counting darkness as light, and the bitter sweet and the sweet bitter …

choices.why: By these words the prophet convicts the sin-draggers of senselessness; it is not God convicting sinners through their foolishness.
rejected: Through their foolishness, God convicts those who have committed sins

choices.term: μὴ πλημμελοῦσιν ἀκαθέκτως ἐπετίθει τὰς δίκας
choices.english: was not laying penalties on them as they sinned without restraint
choices.why: μὴ goes with ἐπετίθει: God was not yet punishing them though they sinned unchecked.
They grew impatient at God's delay, as if wanting the punishment.
Echoes the saying 'be approved money-changers': they prize false coin over true.

choices.english: at the few tears of those who have sinned
choices.why: God turns to mercy even at a few tears.
